hints: Maximum velocity occurs when acceleration equals zero: $25 - t^2 = 0$.
Integrate $a = 25 - t^2$ with respect to $t$ to find the velocity function $v(t)$, using $v(0) = 0$.
Evaluate $v(t)$ at the stationary point $t = 5\text{ s}$.
walkthrough:
Find the time of maximum velocity by setting acceleration to zero for $0 \le t \le 9$:
$$a = 25 - t^2 = 0 \implies t^2 = 25 \implies t = 5\text{ s}$$
Since $\frac{da}{dt} = -2t < 0$, this represents a maximum.

Integrate acceleration to find the velocity function, using the initial condition $v(0) = 0$:
$$v(t) = \int \left(25 - t^2\right) dt = 25t - \frac{1}{3}t^3 + c$$
Since the particle starts from rest, $c = 0$, giving:
$$v(t) = 25t - \frac{1}{3}t^3$$

Substitute $t = 5\text{ s}$ to determine the maximum velocity:
$$v_{\text{max}} = 25(5) - \frac{1}{3}(5^3) = 125 - \frac{125}{3} = \frac{250}{3} = 83\frac{1}{3}\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the condition for maximum velocity: the derivative $\frac{dv}{dt} = a(t) = 0$:
$$25 - t^2 = 0$$
$$t^2 = 25 \implies t = 5\text{ s} \quad (t > 0)$$

Integrate the acceleration function to find velocity:
$$v(t) = \int a(t)\,dt = \int (25 - t^2)\,dt$$
$$v(t) = 25t - \frac{t^3}{3} + c$$
Given $v(0) = 0$, the integration constant is $c = 0$:
$$v(t) = 25t - \frac{1}{3}t^3$$

Substitute $t = 5\text{ s}$ into the velocity equation:
$$v(5) = 25 \times 5 - \frac{1}{3} \times 5^3$$
$$25 \times 5 = 125$$
$$\frac{1}{3} \times 125 = \frac{125}{3}$$
$$v_{\text{max}} = 125 - \frac{125}{3} = \frac{375 - 125}{3} = \frac{250}{3} = 83\frac{1}{3}\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.Integrating Motion Functions: Sets $25 - t^2 = 0 \implies t = 5\text{ s}$, integrates to $v = 25t - \frac{1}{3}t^3$, and evaluates $v(5) = 83\frac{1}{3}\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

hints: Integrate the velocity function $v(t) = 25t - \frac{1}{3}t^3$ from $t = 0$ to the time of maximum velocity $t = 5\text{ s}$.
Evaluate $s(5) - s(0)$ to obtain the distance.
walkthrough:
Integrate the velocity function to find the displacement expression:
$$s(t) = \int \left(25t - \frac{1}{3}t^3\right) dt = \frac{25}{2}t^2 - \frac{1}{12}t^4$$
Since $s(0) = 0$, the constant is zero.

Evaluate the distance travelled from $t = 0$ to $t = 5\text{ s}$:
$$s(5) = \frac{25}{2}(5^2) - \frac{1}{12}(5^4) = \frac{25}{2}(25) - \frac{625}{12}$$
$$s(5) = \frac{625}{2} - \frac{625}{12} = \frac{3750 - 625}{12} = \frac{3125}{12} \approx 260.42\text{ m} \approx 260\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the definite integral for displacement from $t = 0$ to $t = 5\text{ s}$:
$$s = \int_0^5 v(t)\,dt = \int_0^5 \left(25t - \frac{1}{3}t^3\right) dt$$

Substitute the upper limit $t = 5$:
$$\frac{25}{2} \times 5^2 = \frac{25 \times 25}{2} = \frac{625}{2} = 312.5$$
$$\frac{1}{12} \times 5^4 = \frac{625}{12} \approx 52.0833$$
$$s = 312.5 - 52.0833 = 260.4167\text{ m}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $260\text{ m}$ (or exactly $\frac{3125}{12}\text{ m}$).

ai_rubric.Integrating Motion Functions: Integrates $v$ to obtain $s = \frac{25}{2}t^2 - \frac{1}{12}t^4$ and evaluates at $t = 5$ to get $260\text{ m}$.

hints: First, determine the velocity at the transition time $t = 9\text{ s}$ using the first velocity function: $v(9) = 25(9) - \frac{1}{3}(9^3)$.
For $t > 9$, integrate the second acceleration function $a = -3t^{-1/2}$.
The change in velocity is $\Delta v = \int_9^{25} -3t^{-1/2}\,dt = \left[-6t^{1/2}\right]_9^{25}$.
Add this change in velocity to $v(9)$ to find $v(25)$.
walkthrough:
Find the velocity at the boundary time $t = 9\text{ s}$ using the first velocity formula:
$$v(9) = 25(9) - \frac{1}{3}(9^3) = 225 - \frac{729}{3} = 225 - 243 = -18\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the change in velocity between $t = 9$ and $t = 25$ by integrating $a = -3t^{-1/2}$:
$$\Delta v = \int_9^{25} -3t^{-1/2}\,dt = \left[-3\left(\frac{t^{1/2}}{1/2}\right)\right]_9^{25} = \left[-6t^{1/2}\right]_9^{25}$$
$$\Delta v = -6\sqrt{25} - \left(-6\sqrt{9}\right) = -6(5) + 6(3) = -30 + 18 = -12\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Determine the velocity at $t = 25\text{ s}$:
$$v(25) = v(9) + \Delta v = -18 + (-12) = -30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Evaluate the velocity at the transition point $t = 9\text{ s}$:
$$v(9) = 25 \times 9 - \frac{1}{3} \times 9^3$$
$$25 \times 9 = 225$$
$$\frac{1}{3} \times 729 = 243$$
$$v(9) = 225 - 243 = -18\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Integrate the acceleration $a(t) = -3t^{-1/2}$ for $t \ge 9$:
$$v(t) = \int -3t^{-1/2}\,dt = -3 \times \frac{t^{1/2}}{1/2} + C = -6t^{1/2} + C$$

Determine the integration constant $C$ using continuity of velocity at $t = 9\text{ s}$:
$$-18 = -6\sqrt{9} + C$$
$$-18 = -6(3) + C = -18 + C \implies C = 0$$
Therefore, for $t \ge 9$, the velocity function is:
$$v(t) = -6t^{1/2}$$

Substitute $t = 25\text{ s}$ into the velocity equation:
$$v(25) = -6\sqrt{25} = -6 \times 5 = -30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.Integrating Motion Functions: Finds $v(9) = -18\text{ m s}^{-1}$, integrates $-3t^{-1/2}$ to get $\Delta v = -12\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and evaluates $v(25) = -30\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
ai_rubric.Modelling Piecewise Motion: Correctly matches boundary velocity at $t = 9\text{ s}$ across the piecewise acceleration models.
